deep.reconstruction:
Dating and context. The notebook is a list of research problems. The Habilitationsschrift (1886) and the 'Brief an Hermite' (Hilbert corresponded with Hermite c. 1886-88) suggest c. 1887-1889, before the 1890 finiteness paper. The page has four separate items.

(1) Continuation from the previous page. The full sentence reads: 'Alle ganzrationalen Funktionen u = φ(x,y,z,...), v = ψ(x,y,z,...), ... bestimmen, welche [umgekehrt] ganze Funktionen von x,y,z,... sind.' The bracketed word is my reading. In modern terms: determine all polynomial maps F = (φ, ψ, ...): A^n → A^n whose inverse is also polynomial. That is, describe the group Aut(A^n) of polynomial automorphisms (the 'Cremona-type' or tame/wild problem). No derivation is given; it is only a problem statement.

(2) Gordan analogue. Gordan finds systems of binary quadratic forms f_1, f_2, f_3 by requiring:
- the second transvectants (f_i, f_j)_2 = 0 for i ≠ j;
- the (f_i, f_i)_2 are equal, or equal up to sign.
Here (f,g)_2 = f_xx g_yy - 2 f_xy g_xy + f_yy g_xx up to a constant. (f,g)_2 is the polarized discriminant, the unique SL2-invariant bilinear form on the 3-dimensional space of binary quadratics. So Gordan's systems are orthogonal (or orthonormal) bases with respect to the discriminant quadric. This corresponds to SL2 → SO(3) and is used, for example, in Gordan's and Klein's treatment of the icosahedral and quintic problem. Example (mine): f1 = x^2 + y^2, f2 = i(x^2 - y^2), f3 = 2i·xy. These are mutually orthogonal, with (f_k, f_k)_2 = 8 for all k.
Hilbert proposes the analogous problem for ternary linear forms: find systems of linear forms in three variables whose bilinear invariants satisfy the same vanishing or equal-up-to-sign conditions. A bilinear invariant of two ternary linear forms needs a fixed conic or dual quadratic form, so this is presumably meant relative to a quadric. He cross-refers to his letter to Hermite.

(3) 'Alle ein-eindeutigen Transformationen im Raume beliebiger Dimension finden.' Find all one-to-one transformations of n-space. This is either the birational (Cremona) group or the bijective-polynomial version of item (1). It is a problem statement only.

(4) Eigenform problem for the first transvectant, referring to the Habilitationsschrift. Given a binary form f, define the linear operator T(φ) = (f,φ)_1 = f_x φ_y - f_y φ_x. The equation (f,φ)_1 = λφ is an eigenvalue problem. Degrees force f to be quadratic (or λ to be a form of degree n-2); with f quadratic, T preserves the space of forms of each degree.
Hilbert writes φ = C_0 λ^{ν-1} + C_1 λ^{ν-2} + ... and says to 'actually apply the transvection process', i.e. form (f,φ)_1, to get insight into the analytic structure of the covariants C_0, C_1, .... The following reconstruction is mine:
- Let C_{i+1} = (f, C_i)_1 = T^i C_0, and φ = Σ_{i=0}^{ν-1} λ^{ν-1-i} C_i.
- Then λφ - (f,φ)_1 telescopes to C_0 λ^ν - C_ν.
- Hence if T^ν C_0 = μ C_0, i.e. C_ν = μ C_0, every λ with λ^ν = μ gives an eigenform φ.
This is the standard construction of eigenvectors from a cyclic vector. Example: f = xy, C_0 = x^3 + y^3. Then C_1 = -3x^3 + 3y^3 and C_2 = 9 C_0, so ν = 2 and λ = ±3. With λ = 3, φ = 6y^3, which is an eigenform with eigenvalue 3.
For f = xy, T(x^a y^b) = (b - a) x^a y^b, so the eigenforms are the monomials in the linear factors of f.

(5) Closing remark: 'Auch unendlich viele Formen haben nur ein endliches System von Invarianten.' This asserts finiteness of invariant systems even for infinitely many ground forms. It anticipates the 1890 paper, whose Theorem I (the basis theorem) is explicitly stated for infinitely many forms.
errors: Final claim, read literally as finite generation of the joint invariant ring of infinitely many ground forms (infinitely many coefficient variables): false. Joint SL2-invariants of infinitely many binary linear forms include the infinitely many brackets [1j] = a1*bj - a1'*bj', and no finite set generates them. The correct statement is Hilbert's basis theorem: any ideal, even one generated by infinitely many forms in finitely many variables, has a finite basis. Alternatively it holds for families depending on finitely many parameters.

In φ = C_0 λ^{ν-1} + C_1 λ^{ν-2} + ... + C_ν, the last term should be C_{ν-1} (λ^0) for the indexing to be consistent. Otherwise C_ν stands for the term of the relation C_ν = μ C_0. This is a likely notational slip; it may also be a transcription issue.
Ternary linear forms have no bilinear invariant without an auxiliary quadratic form. The proposed analogue is underspecified as written (presumably a fixed conic is understood).

results.what: Problem: determine all polynomial maps of n-space with polynomial inverse (and all one-to-one transformations of n-space)
results.modern_name: Structure of the polynomial automorphism group Aut(A^n) / Cremona group; tame generators problem (cf. Jacobian conjecture)
results.usually_credited_to: Jung (1942) and van der Kulk (1953) for n=2; Keller (1939) Jacobian problem; Nagata (1972) wildness question; Shestakov–Umirbaev (2004) n=3. Cremona transformations: Cremona, Noether (19th c.)

results.what: Gordan's orthogonal systems of binary quadratics via vanishing second transvectants, and a proposed ternary-linear analogue
results.modern_name: Orthogonal bases for the discriminant (Killing) form on binary quadratics ≅ sl2 ≅ so(3); orthonormal frames for a quadric

results.what: Eigenforms of the operator φ ↦ (f,φ)_1, built as polynomials in λ from iterated transvectants C_{i+1}=(f,C_i)_1
results.modern_name: Eigenvectors of the sl2-action of a quadratic (weight vectors); cyclic-vector construction
results.usually_credited_to: Classical invariant theory (Cayley, Sylvester, Gordan); Hilbert's Habilitationsschrift 1886 on invariant properties of special binary forms/Kugelfunktionen

results.what: Finiteness of invariant systems even for infinitely many forms
results.modern_name: Hilbert basis theorem / Hilbert finiteness theorem
